source.data_source: Oracle: OpenFOAM v2412 simpleFoam + Spalart-Allmaras, snappyHexMesh background-on-airfoil ~108k cells, no addLayers (y+ ~ 1000 with wall functions). Alpha sweep at 0/4/8/10/12 deg, M=0.15, Re=6e6, c=1m, U=30 m/s, nu=5e-6.
source.ref_data_source: Ladson 1988 NASA TM-4074, 120-grit zone (Re=6e6, M=0.15, transition tripped at LE). https://tmbwg.github.io/turbmodels/NACA0012_validation/CLCD_Ladson_expdata.dat
source.calibration_note: gt_value comes from the oracle (this repo's solve.sh), not Ladson. Without addLayers the oracle's wall BL is under-resolved → CL underpredicted ~10% at alpha=4 and ~35-50% at alpha=10/12 (premature stall), CD overpredicted 3-9x. CL_alpha slope from oracle is 0.082/deg vs Ladson 0.109/deg. T_good is sized to allow agent runs on similar 50-200k snappy meshes without addLayers; agents that add wall layers will likely score better than the oracle. Re-anchoring against Ladson would require a y+<1 wall-resolved mesh (~1-2M cells) which is out of scope for this oracle's per-trial wall-time budget.
source.calibration_run: 2026-05-11, /work/case alpha sweep on rserver naca0012_dev container
source.sample_points_used: Ladson 120-grit zone; oracle reports at the script-driven angles 0/4/8/10/12 deg (not the experimental angles 4.11/8.08/10.10/12.13 deg).

mesh_cell_count.description: Total cell count of the airfoil mesh (single mesh used across alpha sweep)
mesh_cell_count.T_good_source: Oracle's snappyHexMesh L4-L5 + nearbox/wakebox refinement gives ~108k cells. T_good wide because agents may pick L3-L6 refinement; physics_min=20k filters out single-block airfoil meshes that won't resolve LE.

final_residual_U.description: Final momentum residual at end of alpha=8 deg solve
final_residual_U.T_good_source: Oracle reaches 7e-9 in 1500 iter. Steady SA on attached subsonic airfoil should converge to 1e-5 or better.

CL_at_alpha_4.T_good_source: Oracle CL=0.3945 at alpha=4 deg (vs Ladson 0.4397, oracle 10% low). T_good=0.04 covers ~10% turbulence-model + grid scatter; physics_min=0.2 catches gross under-resolution, physics_max=0.6 catches lift-frame errors that report a near-1.0 value.

CL_at_alpha_10.T_good_source: Oracle CL=0.670 at alpha=10 deg (vs Ladson 1.077, oracle 38% low — premature stall from coarse wall mesh). T_good loose because agents with addLayers will land closer to Ladson 1.0+ and we want both regimes scoring.

CL_at_alpha_12.T_good_source: Oracle CL=0.678 at alpha=12 deg (vs Ladson 1.272). Same stall sensitivity as alpha=10; T_good widened further.

CD_at_alpha_4.T_good_source: Oracle CD=0.0308 at alpha=4 deg (vs Ladson 0.00879, oracle 3.5x high — wall under-resolved + numerical dissipation at LE). physics_min=0.005 catches a y+<1 wall-resolved oracle that reproduces Ladson; physics_max=0.06 catches gross failure.

CD_at_alpha_10.T_good_source: Oracle CD=0.101 at alpha=10 deg (vs Ladson 0.0118, oracle 8.6x high). Same wall under-resolution; physics_min=0.01 to allow well-resolved oracles.

CL_alpha_slope_per_deg.description: Linear-regression slope of CL vs alpha (deg) over alpha=0,4,8 deg
CL_alpha_slope_per_deg.T_good_source: Oracle slope=0.082/deg (vs Ladson 0.109/deg, oracle 25% low — driven by stalled CL@8). Thin-airfoil theory predicts 0.110/deg; well-resolved oracles will exceed this. T_good=0.012 covers oracle-coarse to ladson-grade.
